          "excerpt": "dur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf laesst sie deklariert aus (bead 1jg.2),\n# die Gate-Datei nennt das placement, nicht der Zufall. --ci misst dagegen\n# denselben Satz wie die abgeleitete Workflow (--placement ci): wer den\n# Runner in der gehosteten CI aufruft, darf dort nicht ploetzlich ohne die\n# hosted-Gates dastehen (Befund 2 an bead coding-harness-1jg.3, Review von\n# PR #32). Die Action-Entsprechungen sind dabei REPORT, niemals stilles\n# Auslassen.\nplatzierung=lokal\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && platzierung=ci\ngate_tsv=$(\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --commands --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$platzierung\" --tsv $([ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && echo \"--skip-equivalents\")) \\\n    || { echo \"die Gate-Liste liess sich nicht erzeugen — kein VERIFY ohne gemessene Gates\" >&2; exit 2; }\n[ -n \"$gate_tsv\" ] || { echo \"die Gate-Liste ist leer — ein Job ohne messbare Gates ist ein Konfigurationsfehler\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\necho \"\"\necho \"── gates: job=$JOB ──────────────────────────────────────────────\"\n\n# The commands come out of the one list — id, enforcement, command, per tab.\n# The runner respects the vocabulary: only `block` turns the run red,\n# `report`/`advisory` speak up without blocking.\nfehler=0\nstop_gate=\"\"\nverbleibend=\"\"\nwhile IFS=\"$(printf '\\t')\" read -r gid enf cmd; do\n    [ -z \"$cmd\" ] && continue\n    # Cheap-first stop (bead coding-harness-bxxt.1): after the first blocking\n    # failure no further selected gate runs. The remaining ids are collected\n    # from the already obtained TSV and named in one summary below the loop;\n    # `--ci` never sets stop_gate and keeps running every selected gate.\n    if [ \"$CI_MODE\" -ne 1 ] && [ -n \"$stop_gate\" ]; then\n        verbleibend=\"${verbleibend}${gid}\n\"\n        continue\n    fi\n    # Werkzeuge aus dem Pin aufloesen (gates.md G-12): `python3` in der Liste\n    # heisst \"der gepinnte Interpreter\", nicht \"was der PATH gerade hergibt\".\n    # Die CI macht dasselbe ueber setup-python mit derselben Version.\n    # Quoted for `sh -c`: an absolute path may hold a space; a quote inside it is escaped.\n    python_word=\"'$(printf %s \"$PYTHON\" | sed \"s/'/'\\\\\\\\''/g\")'\"\n    lauf_cmd=${cmd/python3/\"$python_word\"}\n    echo \"\"\n    # Keep machine-local interpreter paths out of logs and repair evidence.\n    echo \"── [$gid] $ $cmd\"\n    # Monotonic readings immediately around the unchanged gate command; the\n    # raw status is captured before any timing operation, so it is the gate\n    # command's own and not a helper's (bead coding-harness-1um6).\n    g_secs=\"\"\n    dur_call g_t0 clock\n    sh -c \"$lauf_cmd\"\n    gate_status=$?\n    dur_call g_t1 clock\n    if [ -n \"$RUN_ID\" ] && [ -n \"$g_t0\" ] && [ -n \"$g_t1\" ]; then\n        dur_call g_secs gate --run \"$RUN_ID\" --gate \"$gid\" --start \"$g_t0\" --end \"$g_t1\" --status \"$gate_status\" --enforcement \"$enf\"\n    fi\n    if [ \"$gate_status\" -eq 0 ]; then\n        echo \"── [$gid] gruen\"\n    elif [ \"$enf\" = \"block\" ]; then\n        fehler=1\n        # `--ci` stays exhaust",

          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",

          "excerpt": "def hold_admission(command: list[str]) -> Iterator[int | None]:\n    \"\"\"One machine admission around protected work: queue, memory gate, published ownership.\n\n    Yields the lock descriptor local children must inherit, or None when this\n    entry is nested in an ancestor's admission. Refusals raise\n    VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body runs; release\n    happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command)\n    try:\n        admission.enter()\n    except BaseException:\n        admission.release()\n        raise\n    try:\n        yield admission.state.lock_fd\n    finally:\n        admission.release()\n",

          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "reference": "The target picture",
          "start_line": 149,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
      ],

          "excerpt": "duration_admission_context() {\n    if [ \"$1\" != \"${HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD:-}\" ]; then\n        unset HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_ID HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_WAIT 2>/dev/null || :\n    fi\n}\n\nif \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock --held >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    # A valid marker means this run nests in an admission an ancestor holds.\n    # One shape is the exception: when our parent IS the supervisor that holds\n    # the admission (the pid the holder published), this runner is the very\n    # command that admission admitted, and its fresh context — measured id and\n    # wait — is ours to record. The helper\n# scripts/verify_duration.py holds no gate command and reads no gate list: it\n# takes monotonic readings around the existing gate command, appends one JSON\n# line per event to the shared state root and refuses substituted\n# destinations. A storage failure warns here and leaves the gates, their\n# enforcement and the verdict untouched; the run then records no history and\n# cannot supply a persisted baseline. The admission supervisor's re-exec above\n# reaches this block once — the nested run inherits its ancestor's admission\n# and marks it reused instead of measuring a second wait.\nDUR_BROKEN=0\n# Runs in the parent shell (a $() subshell could not keep the flag), and\n# stores the helper's stdout in the named variable; the helper's own\n# diagnostics already went to stderr, visibly.\ndur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf laesst sie deklariert aus (bead 1jg.2),\n# die Gate-Datei nennt das placement, nicht der Zufall. --ci misst dagegen\n# denselben Satz wie die abgeleitete Workflow (--placement ci): wer den\n# Runner in der gehosteten CI aufruft, darf dort nicht ploetzlich ohne die\n# hosted-Gates dastehen (Befund 2 an bead coding-harness-1jg.3, Review von\n# PR #32).           "excerpt": "def full_verify(root: Path, env: dict[str, str], key: str | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"`make verify` under one machine admission: the problems, empty when it is green.\n\n    The full check of a repair whose targeted coverage was not safe, and of phase 6's boundary. New\n    files are added intent-to-add for the gates and dropped afterwards; a refusal of the admission,\n    a timeout and a red exit are problems; a `make` that cannot be started raises `CallFailed`.\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission([\"make\", \"verify\"]) as owned:\n            try:\n                intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n            except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n                return [f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before `make verify`: {error}\"]\n            done = launch(\n                [\"make\", \"verify\"],\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except verify_lock.VerifyLockError as error:\n        problems.append(scrub(f\"`make verify` was not started: {error}\", key))\n    except StepTimedOut as error:\n        problems.append(f\"`make verify` did not finish: {error}\")\n    else:\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            problems.append(f\"`make verify` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after `make verify`: {error}\")\n    return problems\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6",

          "excerpt": "def verify_draft(\n    root: Path, ctx: Context, key: str | None, new_adrs: list[str], tools: dict[str, str] | None = None\n) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:\n    \"\"\"A draft attempt's post-run checks: the problems, and whether the answer is owed.\n\n    The order is the spec's (criteria 10 to 16): the ADR count, the derived files, the document check\n    `bash scripts/verify_all.sh --job docs` - its exit code decides; the one missing answer it tolerates\n    is the gate's own, asked for through `check_adr_answers.TOLERATE_ENV`, never read from its output -\n    the two artefacts, the plan card and the `## Time used` heading. Implement keeps full `make verify`;\n    repair takes the targeted check, with the full suite as its fallback and before phase 6.\n    \"\"\"\n    owed = False\n    if len(new_adrs) > 1:\n        problems = [\"the attempt left more than one new ADR file: \" + \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in new_adrs)]\n        return problems, owed\n    tampered = tool_problem(root, tools)\n    if tampered:\n        return [tampered], owed\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n                # The one tolerance of a draft is the gate's own, set by this runner alone: with this\n                # variable `adr-answers` reports this change's missing answer and passes, so the\n                # exit code of the document check decides and no output is read (spec, criterion 13; F-9, F-10).\n                check_adr_answers.TOLERATE_ENV: ctx.change,\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n    preparation = prepare_derived(root, env, key)\n    if preparation:\n        return preparation, owed\n    try:\n        # One machine-wide admission before the timed check: queue and memory waits consume no\n        # step limit; a refusal is a failed check, never a started one (bead coding-harness-p6mu).\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission(DOCS_VERIFY) as owned:\n            done = launch(\n                DOCS_VERIFY,\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except (CallFailed, verify_lock.VerifyLockError) as error:\n        # A document check that cannot start is as failed a post-run check as a red one: its\n        # diagnostics reach the attempt's block, and the chain moves on to the next attempt (2a's F-7).\n        return [f\"`{DOCS_VERIFY_NAME}` could not run: {error}\"], owed\n    problems = []\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        problems.append(f\"`{DOCS_VERIFY_NAME}` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    else:\n        owed = answer_is_owed(root, ctx.change)\n    plan_missing = not ctx.plan.is_file()\n    for name in (\"spec.md\", \"plan.md\"):\n        if not (ctx.folder / name).is_file():\n            problems.append(f\"plans/changes/{ctx.change}/{name} is missing after the draft.\")\n    if not plan_missing:\n        # An absent plan.md is one problem of its own: the card and Time-used checks would read an\n        # empty string and name two faults a missing file cannot have (repair L3-4).\n        plan_text = _read_quietly(ctx.plan)\n        if card_problem(plan_text) is not None:\n            problems.append(CARD_PROBLEM)\n        if not TIME_HEADING.search(plan_text):\n            problems.append(f\"plans/changes/{ctx.change}/plan.md has no `## Time used` heading.\")\n    return problems, owed\n",

          "excerpt": "def _schritt(g: dict[str, Any]) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"Ein YAML-Schritt fuer einen Gate — id, name, run/uses, with, enforcement.\n\n    Jeder Gate-Schritt traegt `if: ${{ !cancelled() }}` (bead\n    coding-harness-bl2): wird ein frueherer Gate rot, setzt dieser Schritt\n    dadurch nicht stumm aus — die CI uebt jeden spaeteren Gate noch aus und\n    faellt am Ende insgesamt. So sagen CI und der lokale Lauf dasselbe.\n    checkout und setup-deps tragen das `if` bewusst nicht: ohne sie hat kein\n    Gate einen Gegenstand.\n    \"\"\"\n    zeilen = [\n        f\"      - name: {g['name']}\",\n        f\"        id: {g['id']}\",\n        \"        if: ${{ !cancelled() }}\",\n    ]\n    if g[\"action\"]:\n        zeilen.append(f\"        uses: {g['action']}\")\n    else:\n        zeilen.append(f\"        run: {g['command']}\")\n    with_block = g.get(\"with\") or {}\n    if with_block:\n        zeilen.append(\"        with:\")\n        for schluessel, wert in with_block.items():\n            teil_zeilen = str(wert).split(\"\\n\")\n            if len(teil_zeilen) > 1:\n                # Block-Literal: ein Wert wie `**/*.md` waere als YAML-Alias\n                # invalid. Das Literal nimmt alles wortwoertlich.\n                zeilen.append(f\"          {schluessel}: |\")\n                for extra in teil_zeilen:\n                    if extra.strip():\n                        zeilen.append(f\"            {extra}\")\n            else:\n                zeilen.append(f\"          {schluessel}: {teil_zeilen[0]}\")\n    if g[\"enforcement\"] in (\"advisory\", \"report\"):\n        zeilen.append(\"        continue-on-error: true\")\n    return zeilen\n",

          "excerpt": "def generate_ci() -> str:\n    \"\"\"Die abgeleitete ci.yml — deterministisch, aus der einen Liste.\"\"\"\n    alle = gates()\n    versionen = interpreters()\n    # Quoted: an unquoted `3.10` is the number 3.1 to YAML. Built outside the f-string\n    # below, which may not reuse its own quotes before Python 3.12.\n    matrix = \", \".join(f'\"{v}\"' for v in versionen)\n    # Bead 1jg.2: writer-only Gates misst nur die Schreibmaschine — die\n    # abgeleitete ci.yml haelt sie deklariert raus, statt sie dort unmoeglich\n    # laufen zu lassen. Ein writer-only Gate mit needs_tracker stoesst folglich\n    # auch keine Hydratation an.\n    pruefe = [g for g in alle if g[\"job\"] == \"verify\" and misst_in(g, \"ci\")]\n    drift = [g for g in alle if g[\"job\"] == \"drift\" and misst_in(g, \"ci\")]\n    aktionen = [g for g in pruefe if g[\"action\"]]\n    kommandos = [g for g in pruefe if not g[\"action\"]]\n    zeilen: list[str] = [\n        \"name: verify\",\n        \"\",\n        \"# GENERATED by `python3 scripts/ci_gates.py --generate-ci` from decisions/gates.yaml (D-10).\",\n        \"# Hand-edits fail the ci-drift gate on purpose.\",\n        \"\",\n        \"on:\",\n        \"  push:\",\n        f\"    branches: [{MAIN_BRANCH}]\",\n        \"  pull_request:\",\n        # The merge queue (bead coding-harness-eh42) builds a group's merge ref and asks for the\n        # required check `verify` there; without this trigger a queued PR waits forever.\n        \"  merge_group:\",\n        \"    types: [checks_requested]\",\n        \"  schedule:\",\n        '    - cron: \"23 4 * * *\"',\n        \"  workflow_dispatch:\",\n        \"\",\n        \"concurrency:\",\n        \"  group: verify-${{ github.event_name }}-${{ github.ref }}\",\n        \"  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}\",\n        \"\",\n        \"jobs:\",\n        f\"  {MATRIX_JOB}:\",\n        \"    if: github.event_name == 'push' || github.event_name == 'pull_request' || github.event_name == 'merge_group'\",\n        # One leg per declared interpreter, and no fail-fast: a red leg must not\n        # cancel the other, for the reason bead coding-harness-bl2 gave for steps.\n        \"    strategy:\",\n        \"      fail-fast: false\",\n        \"      matrix:\",\n        f\"        python: [{matrix}]\",\n        \"    runs-on: ubuntu-latest\",\n        \"    steps:\",\n        *_checkout(pruefe),\n        *_toolchain(\"${{ matrix.python }}\"),\n    ]\n    # Bead coding-harness-4t8: der Schritt gehoert nur i",

          "excerpt": "duration_admission_context() {\n    if [ \"$1\" != \"${HARNESS_VERIFY_LOCK_HELD:-}\" ]; then\n        unset HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_ID HARNESS_VERIFY_ADMISSION_WAIT 2>/dev/null || :\n    fi\n}\n\nif \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock --held >/dev/null 2>&1; then\n    # A valid marker means this run nests in an admission an ancestor holds.\n    # One shape is the exception: when our parent IS the supervisor that holds\n    # the admission (the pid the holder published), this runner is the very\n    # command that admission admitted, and its fresh context — measured id and\n    # wait — is ours to record. Every genuinely nested run drops that context\n    # here, so its helpers resolve the shared wait from the validated\n    # ownership record and mark it reused instead of passing the ancestor's\n    # admission off as their own (bead coding-harness-1um6).\n    duration_admission_context \"$PPID\"\nelse\n    exec \"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_lock -- bash \"$PWD/scripts/verify_all.sh\" ${ORIGINAL_ARGS[@]+\"${ORIGINAL_ARGS[@]}\"}\nfi\n\n# ── Measured durations (bead coding-harness-1um6) ──────────────────────────\n#\n# One run identity per admitted runner, created here — after admission, before\n# the report and gate selection, so execution seconds cover both. The helper\n# scripts/verify_duration.py holds no gate command and reads no gate list: it\n# takes monotonic readings around the existing gate command, appends one JSON\n# line per event to the shared state root and refuses substituted\n# destinations. A storage failure warns here and leaves the gates, their\n# enforcement and the verdict untouched; the run then records no history and\n# cannot supply a persisted baseline. The admission supervisor's re-exec above\n# reaches this block once — the nested run inherits its ancestor's admission\n# and marks it reused instead of measuring a second wait.\nDUR_BROKEN=0\n# Runs in the parent shell (a $() subshell could not keep the flag), and\n# stores the helper's stdout in the named variable; the helper's own\n# diagnostics already went to stderr, visibly.\ndur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf laesst sie deklariert aus (bead 1jg.2),\n# die Gate-Datei nennt das placement, nicht der Zufall. --ci misst dagegen\n# denselben Satz wie die abgeleitete Workflow (--placement ci): wer den\n# Runner in der gehosteten CI aufruft, darf dort nicht ploetzlich ohne die\n# hosted-Gates dastehen (Befund 2 an bead coding-harness-1jg.3, Review von\n# PR #32). Die Action-Entsprechungen sind dabei REPORT, niemals stilles\n# Auslassen.\nplatzierung=lokal\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && platzierung=ci\ngate_tsv=$(\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --commands --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$platzierung\" --tsv $([ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && echo \"--skip-equivalents\")) \\\n    || { echo \"die Gate-Liste liess sich nicht erzeugen — kein VERIFY ohne gemessene Gates\" >&2; exit 2; }\n[ -n \"$gate_tsv\" ] || { echo \"die Gate-Liste ist leer — ein Job ohne messbare Gates ist ein Konfigurationsfehler\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\necho \"\"",

          "excerpt": "def _targeted_body(\n    root: Path,\n    plan: Path,\n    env: dict[str, str],\n    key: str | None,\n    formatted: list[str] | None,\n    tools: dict[str, str] | None,\n    accepted_plan: bytes | None,\n    previous_failures: Sequence[str],\n    against: str,\n    scope: list[str] | None,\n    clearing: ClearingEvidence | None = None,\n) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"A repair's post-run checks in targeted mode: the shared preparation, then the targeted or full check.\n\n    Everything before the selection - format, cheap checks, ledger clearing, derived preparation - is\n    `verify_attempt`'s own, run outside the admission and without its marker. The selection follows\n    the preparation, so generated files are in it; a coverage that cannot be determined safely runs the\n    admitted full check instead. A passing result is never worded as full verification. The clearing\n    capture covers the fallback too: the clearing happened in the shared preparation, before the\n    selection chose the admitted full check.\n    \"\"\"\n    # Nothing a targeted run starts carries or claims the verify admission.\n    env = {name: value for name, value in env.items() if name not in (verify_lock.LOCK_ENV, verify_lock.TOKEN_ENV)}\n\n    def ledger(error: BaseException) -> list[str]:\n        return [\n            f\"the criterion ledger of {plan.name} could not be updated: {getattr(error, 'strerror', None) or error}\"\n        ]\n\n    try:\n        line = format_step(root, env, key, tools, inherit_admission=False)\n        if formatted is not None and line is not None:\n            formatted.append(line)\n    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as error:\n        return ledger(error)\n    try:\n        cheap = cheap_checks(root, env, plan, key, accepted_plan, previous_failures)\n    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as error:\n        return [protect_diagnostics(f\"{CHEAP_LABEL}: the cheap checks could not run: {error}\", key)]\n    if cheap:\n        return [f\"{CHEAP_LABEL}: {entry}\" for entry in cheap]\n    try:\n        capture_ledger_clearing(root, plan, clearing)\n    except (OSError, RuntimeError, ValueError) as error:\n        return ledger(error)\n    preparation = prepare_derived(root, env, key)\n    if preparation:\n        return preparation\n    chosen = targeted_selection(root, env, against)\n    if chosen.fallback is not None:\n        # Keep the selected scope even if the full check raises before returning its result.\n        if scope is not None:\n            scope.append(fallback_text(chosen.fallback, \"not completed\"))\n        problems = full_verify(root, env, key)\n        if scope is not None:\n            scope[-1] = fallback_text(chosen.fallback, \"red\" if problems else \"green\")\n        return problems\n    problems = []\n    notes: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        try:\n            intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before the checks: {error}\")\n        else:\n            try:\n                problems, notes = run_targeted(root, env, key, chosen)\n            except StepTimedOut as error:\n                problems.append(\n                    protect_diagnostics(f\"{TARGETED_LABEL}: targeted check exceeded its time bound: {error}\", key)\n                )\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after the checks: {error}\")\n    if scope is not None:\n        scope.append(scope_text(chosen, \"red\" if problems else \"green\", notes))\n    return problems\n",

          "excerpt": "def cmd_start(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create one run identity and append its start record with the machine context.\"\"\"\n    memory = verify_lock.read_available_memory()\n    porcelain = _git([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n    event = {\n        \"v\": EVENT_VERSION,\n        \"event\": RUN_START,\n        \"run_id\": uuid.uuid4().hex,\n        \"utc\": _utc_now(),\n        \"repository\": str(Path.cwd()),\n        \"commit\": _git([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"]),\n        # None means git could not answer; only an answer decides yes or no.\n        \"dirty\": None if porcelain is None else bool(porcelain),\n        \"config_sha256\": _gate_file_digest(),\n        \"job\": args.job,\n        \"placement\": args.placement,\n        \"memory_pct\": memory,\n        \"workers\": _worker_setting(),\n        **_context_fields(),\n    }\n    append_event(event)\n    print(event[\"run_id\"])\n    return 0\n",

          "excerpt": "def append_event(event: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one complete JSON line under a file lock, so concurrent runs never mix identities.\"\"\"\n    line = json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True) + \"\\n\"\n    fd = _open_history()\n    try:\n        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n        try:\n            data = line.encode(\"utf-8\")\n            if os.write(fd, data) != len(data):\n                raise StorageUnusable(\"the history write was incomplete; refusing to claim a complete event\")\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the history lock or write failed ({error}); refusing to record event\") from error\n    finally:\n        os.close(fd)\n",

          "excerpt": "def gates() -> list[dict[str, Any]]:\n    \"\"\"Alle Gates der einen Liste, in ihrer Reihenfolge.\"\"\"\n    fehler = validate_schema()\n    if fehler:\n        raise ValueError(\"Gate-Datei verletzt das Schema: \" + \"; \".join(fehler))\n    doc = yaml.safe_load(GATE_FILE.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\"))\n    out: list[dict[str, Any]] = []\n    for g in doc[\"gates\"]:\n        aktion = g.get(\"action\")\n        kommando = g.get(\"command\")\n        ersatz = _lokales_kommando(aktion, g.get(\"with\")) if aktion else None\n        out.append(\n            {\n                \"id\": g[\"id\"],\n                \"name\": g[\"title\"],\n                \"job\": g[\"job\"],\n                \"command\": kommando if kommando else ersatz,\n                \"action\": aktion,\n                \"with\": g.get(\"with\") or {},\n                \"enforcement\": g[\"enforcement\"],\n                \"floor\": g[\"floor\"],\n                \"placement\": g[\"placement\"],\n                \"cost\": g[\"cost\"],\n                \"needs_tracker\": bool(g.get(\"needs_tracker\")),\n                \"needs_history\": bool(g.get(\"needs_history\")),\n                \"subsets\": list(g.get(\"subsets\") or []),\n                \"reason\": g.get(\"reason\", \"\"),\n                \"local_runnable\": kommando is not None or ersatz is not None,\n                \"via_local_equivalent\": ersatz is not None,\n            }\n        )\n    return out\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py::plan_reuse",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "citation": "docs/WORKFLOW.md::Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "### Change classes, the ADR question and decision pull requests\n\nEvery change says in its spec header what kind of change it is — `class:`,\none of four:\n\n- `spike` — answers a question; its output is a recommendation.\n- `bounded` — changes an existing, readable flow without deciding anything new.\n- `feature` — a self-contained deliverable that changes what the system must\n  do or how it is checked.\n- `architectural` — a new subsystem or a break of an interface; it carries its\n  ADR already, so it is not asked.\n\n**The design phase 2b goes by class** (decision D-14,\n`prompts/02b-design.md`): an `architectural` change always runs it; a `feature`\nruns it or says in one sentence of its `spec.md` why not; a `bounded` change\nand a `spike` never run it. Nothing checks this until the change-artefact\nvalidator lands (bead coding-harness-jc3); the review before the merge holds\nit.\n\n**The interview goes by class too** (maintainer, 2026-10-08): a `feature`\nowes at least three distinct, substantive questions; creating or changing an\nADR (one it claims under `adr_files`) raises the debt to five in whatever class the change carries; a `spike`\nowes its three topics or a reasoned skip; a `bounded` change one answered\nquestion or a reasoned skip. What the gate counts and what the review judges\nstands in §2, the paragraph after the phase table.\n\n**Only a `feature` owes an answer to the ADR question:** is this change an\narchitecture decision that needs an ADR? The spec author proposes, in the same\nheader: `change: <folder name>` and `adr_question: {proposed: \"yes\"|\"no\",\nreason: \"<one sentence>\"}` (`prompts/02-spec.md`). The proposal only proposes.\nThe maintainer answers, and the answer lives in\n`decisions/answers/<change>/adr.yaml`, in the format of the LakeSwitch pilot\n(`schema_version: 1`), so LakeSwitch reads it unchanged.\n\nThere are two ways to answer, both through `python3 scripts/harness.py decide\nadr`:\n\n1. **Typed in a terminal** by the maintainer: the command shows each open\n   question with its title, anchor and proposal, takes `y` or `n` and a\n   one-sentence reason, and asks for three explain-back lines at the end.\n2. **Stated in the conversation**, and recorded by the agent exactly as stated,\n   one change per run: `--change <name> --answer yes|no --reason \"<English\n   sentence>\" --stated-in \"<where the maintainer said it>\"`. The source goes\n   into the commit message, not into the answer file.\n\nEither way the command writes the answer files and a commit message, and\nstages, commits and merges nothing. The gate `adr-answers`\n(`scripts/check_adr_answers.py`, in `decisions/gates.yaml`) holds every\nfeature, active or archived, to an answer file that exists, has the format and\nnames its own change.\n\n**A decision takes effect when the maintainer merges its pull request**, or\nasks an agent in the conversation to merge it. There is no commit signing in\nCoding Harness (ADR 0008, 2026-09-30). A pull request that adds, changes or\nremoves a file `provenance.yaml` reserves for `human-decided` — an ADR, an ADR\nanswer, the rule set — is a **decision pull request**: its title is\n`decide(<scope>): <the decision as a statement>`, it carries the label\n`decision`, and its body begins with the block from\n`.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/decision.md` — what is decided, that the merge\nis the confirmation, what it confirms, the options and what follows. Every\nother pull request takes `.github/pull_request_template.md`, whose first lines\nsay that nothing is decided. How an agent merges on request is in\n`prompts/07-commit.md`, \"The merge\".\n\nWhat this does not do:\n\n- The gate holds existence and format only. It cannot see who wrote an answer\n  or who merged it.\n- Agents act under the maintainer's GitHub account, so nobody can tell from\n  GitHub who pressed merge. The merge rule is a rule, not proof.\n- The ask rules in `.claude/settings.json` are a brake against an accidental\n  merge, not a lock. Since the night-stall-guard change (2026-11-09) they match\n  precise",

          "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing};           "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## Six layers\n\n| # | Layer | What it holds | Where |\n| --- | --- | --- | --- |\n| 1 | Every criterion names its proof | Each acceptance criterion in `spec.md` says what refutes it. The plan's `## Criterion ledger` names the test that proves it. A gate turns red when that test disappears. | `spec.md`, `plan.md`, gate `criterion-ledger` (`scripts/check_criterion_ledger.py`) |\n| 2 | Red first | A repair of code counts only when its test fails on the code before the repair. The runner checks this itself: it runs the named test alone against the old code in a temporary worktree. | [Repairing taken findings](WORKFLOW.md#repairing-taken-findings-repair) |\n| 3 | One gate list | `make verify` and the hosted CI run the same list. `scripts/verify_all.sh` asks `scripts/ci_gates.py`, and that reads [`decisions/gates.yaml`](../decisions/gates.yaml). `ci.yml` is generated from the same file, and a hand edit fails the gate `ci-drift`. | [Verification](WORKFLOW.md#verification-runs-through-git-and-ci-not-through-the-harness), [gate catalog](governance/gate-catalog.md) |\n| 4 | The gates test themselves | Every gate has a mutation test: a run that turns red when the thing the gate protects is broken. A gate without one needs a reason in a list that may only shrink (rule RB-G4). An empty set is no result: every gate asserts that what it measured is not empty (rule RB-G7). | [Rule table](governance/regelwerk.md), `scripts/mutation_evidence.py`, `tests/test_ci.py` |\n| 5 | A locked environment | Each checkout builds its own `.venv` from a lock with a hash for every package. Pinned outside tools are tested as the real program against offline contracts, not as expected arguments. A local green means what a CI green means. | `requirements-ci.txt`, `make venv` |\n| 6 | The kit probe | The probe copies everything the kit manifest marks as mechanism into an empty repository and runs the tests there. A red case must be listed with its reason, or the gate `leerprobe` blocks. This is how \"the workflow can be handed over\" becomes a run. | `scripts/kit/probe.py`, `scripts/kit/manifest.yaml` |\n\nLayer 1 is a trust rule against models. A model cannot make a red test go away\nwithout a visible edit of the plan. Layer 2 stops the most common weak repair,\na test that would have passed anyway.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",
          "kind": "local",

New\n    files are added intent-to-add for the gates and dropped afterwards; a refusal of the admission,\n    a timeout and a red exit are problems; a `make` that cannot be started raises `CallFailed`.\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission([\"make\", \"verify\"]) as owned:\n            try:\n                intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n            except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n                return [f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before `make verify`: {error}\"]\n            done = launch(\n                [\"make\", \"verify\"],\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except verify_lock.VerifyLockError as error:\n        problems.append(scrub(f\"`make verify` was not started: {error}\", key))\n    except StepTimedOut as error:\n        problems.append(f\"`make verify` did not finish: {error}\")\n    else:\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            problems.append(f\"`make verify` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after `make verify`: {error}\")\n    return problems\n",

          "excerpt": "def run_targeted(root: Path, env: dict[str, str], key: str | None, chosen: Targeted) -> tuple[list[str], list[str]]:\n    \"\"\"Run the selected targeted commands outside the verify admission: (blocking problems, reported notes).\n\n    Order: ruff over the touched files, pytest over the whole test files, then the selected gates in\n    declaration order through the locked interpreter. The first blocking\n    red, launch error or timeout ends the run with one bounded, protected diagnostic; a gate that only\n    reports or advises is noted and never blocks, as in the local runner. A missing tool is red.\n    \"\"\"\n    limit = f\"the runner's tool limit after {TOOL_SECONDS // 60} minutes\"\n    if chosen.ruff:\n        problem = _cheap_ruff(root, env, key, chosen.ruff)\n        if problem:\n            return [f\"{TARGETED_LABEL}: {problem}\"], []\n    python = root / PYTEST[0]\n    if (chosen.tests or chosen.gates) and not python.is_file():\n        return [\n            protect_diagnostics(f\"{TARGETED_LABEL}: no interpreter at `{PYTEST[0]}`; `make venv` builds it.\", key)\n        ], []\n    if chosen.tests:\n        identity = \"`\" + \" \".join(PYTEST) + \"`\"\n        try:\n            done = launch(\n                [*PYTEST, *chosen.tests],\n                root,\n                targeted_pytest_env(root, env),\n                key,\n                timeout=TARGETED_PYTEST_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's targeted-test limit after {TARGETED_PYTEST_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n            )\n        except (StepTimedOut, CallFailed) as error:\n            return [protect_diagnostics(f\"{TARGETED_LABEL}: {identity} could not be run: {error}\", key)], []\n        if done.returncode:\n            return [f\"{TARGETED_LABEL}: {identity} exited {done.returncode}\\n{_cheap_evidence(done, key)}\"], []\n    notes: list[str] = []\n    gate_env = {**env, \"PYTHON\": str(python), \"PATH\": os.pathsep.join([str(python.parent), env.get(\"PATH\", \"\")])}\n    for gate in chosen.gates:\n        command = str(gate[\"command\"])\n        command = _parse_gate_command(shlex.split(command)).locked_command(python, command)\n        identity = f\"gate `{gate['id']}` ({gate['enforcement']})\"\n        blocking = gate[\"enforcement\"] == \"blo",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py::plan_reuse",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",

          "end_line": 180,
          "excerpt": "def append_event(event: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one complete JSON line under a file lock, so concurrent runs never mix identities.\"\"\"\n    line = json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True) + \"\\n\"\n    fd = _open_history()\n    try:\n        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n        try:\n            data = line.encode(\"utf-8\")\n            if os.write(fd, data) != len(data):\n                raise StorageUnusable(\"the history write was incomplete; refusing to claim a complete event\")\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the history lock or write failed ({error}); refusing to record event\") from error\n    finally:\n        os.close(fd)\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/verify_duration.py",
          "reference": "append_event",

          "excerpt": "## Acceptance criteria\n\n1. When a runner repair has determinable targeted coverage, its post-run\n   verification uses the targeted check instead of full `make verify`.\n   *Refuted by:* a narrow, covered Python repair invoking full verification.\n\n2. When a targeted repair is checked, every surviving touched test file and\n   every surviving linked test file is executed in full from current content.\n   *Refuted by:* an unchanged linked test's failing sibling being omitted,\n   an untracked or index-only touch being missed, a removed path losing its\n   baseline-linked tests, or a retry losing an earlier retained edit.\n\n3. When a repair touches surviving Python files, read-only ruff lint and\n   format checks cover those files after the runner's existing formatting.\n   *Refuted by:* accepting a touched file with a remaining lint or format\n   fault because it was outside the check's targets.\n\n4. When targeted verification runs, it measures the existing locally\n   runnable gates applicable to the touched file kinds with their declared\n   enforcement unchanged.\n   *Refuted by:* omitting the document gates after derived plan/index edits,\n   omitting a changed gate's own check, or treating an unmeasured blocking\n   gate as passing.\n\n5. If a repair touches `prompts/` or its targeted coverage cannot be\n   determined safely, full `make verify` is required for that attempt.\n   *Refuted by:* targeted acceptance of a prompt edit, an unclassified input,\n   an unreadable link inventory or production code with no linked test.\n\n6. When targeted post-run commands execute, they run outside the\n   machine-wide verify admission.\n   *Refuted by:* a targeted command acquiring or claiming inherited ownership\n   of that admission; full fallback and phase-6 checks still owe admission.\n\n7. If a required targeted command fails, cannot start or exceeds its time\n   bound, the repair cannot checkpoint or mark its findings fixed.\n   *Refuted by:* a checkpoint or fixed row despite that failure, or an\n   unbounded/unprotected diagnostic reaching the existing retry flow.\n\n8. When repair uses targeted verification, the existing preparation,\n   accepted-ledger/retry selections, fixed-line validation and red-first\n   proof remain prerequisites for its checkpoint.\n   *Refuted by:* a missing derived refresh, a planted ledger-selected failure\n   being skipped, acceptance of an invalid fixed answer, or a proof failure\n   becoming a fixed row merely because targeted commands passed.\n\n9.           "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",

          "excerpt": "## What was measured\n\nSource: the run log the duration spike added\n(`~/.local/state/coding-harness/verify-duration.jsonl`, bead\ncoding-harness-1um6), read on 2026-11-09 at 22:10 UTC. Only the full job is counted (`job: verify`, 151 runs);\nthe 27 document-only runs are left out.\n\n| Day (UTC) | Full runs | Green | Red | No end record | Wait, hours | Execution, hours | Median wait, min |\n|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 2026-11-04 (from 13:13) | 3 | 3 | 0 | 0 | 1.3 | 1.0 | 25 |\n| 2026-11-05 | 7 | 7 | 0 | 0 | 1.2 | 2.5 | 15 |\n| 2026-11-06 | 25 | 20 | 5 | 0 | 13.2 | 9.8 | 30 |\n| 2026-11-07 | 39 | 30 | 9 | 0 | 21.4 | 14.2 | 30 |\n| 2026-11-08 | 43 | 31 | 12 | 0 | 21.5 | 16.2 | 22 |\n| 2026-11-09 (to 21:42) | 34 | 18 | 10 | 6 | 18.7 | 13.3 | 28 |\n| **Sum** | **151** | **109** | **36** | **6** | **77.3** | **57.1** | 26 (all runs) |\n\nFurther readings from the same log:\n\n- **Runs per change.** The 151 runs belong to 21 worktrees: median 7 full\n  runs per worktree, 11 worktrees with 7 or more, the largest 19\n  (`go-wire-apis`). A change that is checked seven times costs about two and\n  a half hours of execution before any waiting.\n- **Duration.** A green run took 1,230–1,250 s (median per day) on\n  2026-11-04/05 and 1,374 s on 2026-11-09 — about 10 % more in five days.\n  The pytest gate is about four fifths of it\n  ([baseline note](2026-11-04-verify-duration-baseline.md)).\n- **Growth.** `tests/*.py` held 13,168 lines on 2026-10-07, 66,501 on\n  2026-11-07 (both from bead coding-harness-1ga5) and 73,080 lines in 77\n  files at `01fb3e38` (2026-11-09).           "citation": "docs/adr/0025-targeted-check-after-repair.md::Decision",
          "end_line": 70,
          "excerpt": "## Decision\n\nADR 0021 decision 6's last sentence is replaced by:\n\n1. After a runner repair the runner runs a targeted check: the tests linked\n   to the touched files, the prior retry selections, ruff on the touched\n   Python files, and the gates the touched file kinds feed.\n2. When that selection is not safe, the full `make verify` runs instead, as\n   the fallback for that repair.\n3. One fresh green full `make verify` on the head under review is required\n   before phase 6. A red, unstartable or timed-out run stops the review;\n   runner audit lines in `findings.md` do not count as a new head.\n4. The orchestrator measures repair duration, verify-lock wait and every\n   failure the full check before phase 6 finds that a targeted check missed,\n   over five changes or two weeks, whichever comes first, and reports the\n   result to the maintainer.\n5. This rule holds from the merge. The testing-strategy spike (bead\n   coding-harness-1ga5) may amend or replace it with an ADR of its own; the\n   measurement of point 4 enters that spike as a finding.\n\nThe rest of ADR 0021 decision 6 stands unchanged.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/adr/0025-targeted-check-after-repair.md",
          "reference": "Decision",
          "start_line": 49,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },
        {
          "citation": "plans/changes/repair-targeted-check/spec.md::criterion 9",
          "end_line": 114,
          "excerpt": "9. When phase 6 is requested, the runner obtains a fresh green full\n   `make verify` for the current head before starting the reviewer.\n   *Refuted by:* a reviewer call after a red, unstartable or timed-out full\n   check, after the checked head or substantive tree changed, or using only\n   an earlier repair's green result.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, en",

          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",

          "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "def test_runner_reports_each_gate_duration_and_raw_result(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Criterion 1: a finished gate shows its measured seconds beside its verdict.\n\n    Fault this pins: an advisory failure reported without a duration or\n    labelled passed, an unexecuted gate presented as measured, or a gate record\n    losing its raw exit status in history. A blocking failure stops the run —\n    delta is named as not run and leaves no history event (cheap-first, bead\n    coding-harness-bxxt.1).\n    \"\"\"\n    base = tmp_path / \"durations\"\n    order = base / \"order.txt\"\n    tree = _runner_tree_files(base / \"tree\")\n\n    def gate(gid: str, enforcement: str, ending: str) -> dict:\n        return {\n            \"id\": gid,\n            \"title\": f\"The {gid} gate\",\n            \"command\": f'echo {gid} >> \"{order}\"; {ending}',\n            \"job\": \"verify\",\n            \"cost\": \"seconds\",\n            \"enforcement\": enforcement,\n            \"floor\": True,\n            \"placement\": \"both\",\n            \"reason\": \"a duration seed for the runner tree\",\n        }\n\n    _write_gate_file(\n        tree,\n        [\n            gate(\"alpha\", \"block\", \"true\"),\n            gate(\"beta\", \"advisory\", \"exit 1\"),\n            gate(\"gamma\", \"block\", \"exit 1\"),\n            gate(\"delta\", \"block\", \"true\"),\n        ],\n    )\n    _interpreter_wrapper(tree / \".venv\" / \"bin\" / \"python3\", \"venv\", base / \"log\")\n    done = _run_runner(tree, tmp_path / \"home\", [])\n    assert done.returncode == 1, f\"exit {done.returncode}\\n{done.stdout}\\n{done.stderr}\"\n    assert \"VERIFY RED\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    assert \"── [beta] rot, aber nur advisory\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    assert \"── [gamma] RED (block)\" in done.stdout, done.stdout\n    # Every executed gate — passing, advisory-failing and blocking-failing\n    # alike — shows its measured seconds beside its verdict. delta is not\n    # executed: gamma's blocking failure stopped the run before it.\n    for gid in (\"alpha\", \"beta\", \"gamma\"):\n        assert re.search(rf\"── \\[{gid}\\] [0-9]+\\.[0-9]+s\", done.stdout), done.stdout\n    assert order.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"alpha\\nbeta\\ngamma\\n\"\n    assert \"──   [delta] not run\" in done.stdout, \"the stop did not name the gate it did not run\"\n\n    events = _tree_history(tree)\n    starts = [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"run_start\"]\n    assert len(starts) == 1 and starts[0][\"job\"] == \"verify\" and starts[0][\"placement\"] == \"local\"\n    run_id = starts[0][\"run_id\"]\n    gate_events = [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"gate\"]\n    assert len(gate_events) == 3, gate_events\n    gate_rows = {e[\"gate\"]: e for e in gate_events}\n    assert set(gate_rows) == {\"alpha\", \"beta\", \"gamma\"}, gate_rows\n    assert all(row[\"run_id\"] == run_id for row in gate_rows.values())\n    assert gate_rows[\"beta\"][\"exit\"] == 1 and gate_rows[\"beta\"][\"enforcement\"] == \"advisory\", gate_rows[\"beta\"]\n    assert gate_rows[\"gamma\"][\"exit\"] == 1\n    assert all(isinstance(row[\"seconds\"], int | float) and row[\"seconds\"] >= 0 for row in gate_rows.values())\n    ends = [e for e in events if e[\"event\"] == \"run_end\"]\n    assert len(ends) == 1 and ends[0][\"run_id\"] == run_id and ends[0][\"verdict\"] == \"red\"\n",
