          "excerpt": "def _verify_row(tokens: list[str], pid: str, elapsed: str) -> ProcessRow | None:\n    head = Path(tokens[0]).name\n    if head == \"make\":\n        arguments = iter(tokens[1:])\n        options = True\n        for token in arguments:\n            if options and token == \"--\":\n                options = False\n                continue\n            if options and token in {\n                \"-C\",\n                \"-f\",\n                \"-I\",\n                \"-o\",\n                \"-W\",\n                \"--directory\",\n                \"--file\",\n                \"--makefile\",\n                \"--include-dir\",\n                \"--old-file\",\n                \"--assume-old\",\n                \"--what-if\",\n                \"--new-file\",\n                \"--assume-new\",\n                \"--eval\",\n            }:\n                next(arguments, None)\n                continue\n            if options and token.startswith(\"-\"):\n                continue\n            if token == \"verify\":\n                return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=\"verify\", change=NOT_READ)\n        return None\n    if head in SHELLS:\n        # The shell is a wrapper unless it directly runs the verify script itself.\n        arguments = iter(tokens[1:])\n        for token in arguments:\n            if token == \"--\":\n                token = next(arguments, \"\")\n            elif token in {\"-o\", \"+o\", \"-O\", \"+O\"}:\n                next(arguments, None)\n                continue\n            elif token.startswith((\"-\", \"+\")):\n                if token.startswith(\"-\") and not token.startswith(\"--\") and (\"c\" in token or \"s\" in token):\n                    return None  # command text or stdin, not a script invocation\n                continue\n            if _is_verify_script(token):\n                return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=\"verify\", change=NOT_READ)\n            break\n        return None\n    if _is_verify_script(tokens[0]):\n        return ProcessRow(pid=pid, elapsed=elapsed, label=\"verify\", change=NOT_READ)\n    return None\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_process_filter_emits_only_permitted_fields(tmp_path: Path, capsys) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Fault: an option hides a supported runner invocation, a substring match adds unrelated\n    processes, or command arguments beyond pid, label, change and elapsed leak (spec criterion 8).\"\"\"\n    root = tmp_path\n    make_change(root, \"run-report\", plan=plan_text(), findings=\"\")\n    listing = ps_output(\n        \"    1 00:01:02 python3 scripts/stage2.py implement run-report\",\n        \"    2 00:02:03 python3 scripts/stage2.py implement --stage2-off reason run-report\",\n        \"    3 00:30:00 make verify\",\n        \"    4 1-02:03:04 bash scripts/verify_all.sh\",\n        \"    9 00:00:10 python3 scripts/stage2.py draft run-report\",\n        \"    5 00:01:00 vim scripts/stage2.py implement\",  # an editor, not an invocation\n        \"    6 00:01:00 bash -c make verify\",  # a shell wrapper\n        \"    7 00:01:00 tail -f scripts/stage2.py\",  # a reader of the file\n        \"    8 00:10:00 echo SENTINEL-COMMAND run-report\",  # an unrelated command\n    )\n    run = fake_run({PS_ARGV: listing})\n    proc = proc_fixture(tmp_path)\n    code, out = run_main(root, capsys, run=run, proc_dir=proc)\n    assert code == 0\n    live = \"\\n\".join(blocks(out)[\"live\"])\n    for row in [\n        \"pid 1 · implement · change run-report · elapsed 00:01:02\",\n        \"pid 2 · implement · change run-report · elapsed 00:02:03\",  # the option hides nothing\n        \"pid 3 · verify · change not read · elapsed 00:30:00\",\n        \"pid 4 · verify · change not read · elapsed 1-02:03:04\",\n        \"pid 9 · draft · change run-report · elapsed 00:00:10\",\n    ]:\n        assert f\"    {row}\" in live\n    for absent in (\"pid 5\", \"pid 6\", \"pid 7\", \"pid 8\", \"vim\", \"tail\", \"echo\", \"SENTINEL-COMMAND\", \"--stage2-off\"):\n        assert absent not in live\n",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py::plan_reuse",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",
          "kind": "local",

          "excerpt": "def test_reuse_requires_the_exact_binding_seat_model_and_prompt(store, repo):\n    k = key(\"s1\")\n    make_source(store, repo, results=[(k, terminal(k))])\n    source, plan = resume(store, repo, [k])\n    assert source.usable and set(plan.reused) == {\"s1\"} and plan.not_reused == []\n    assert plan.reused[\"s1\"][\"report\"] == \"REPORT\"\n    for field, other in [\n        (\"stage\", \"map\"),\n        (\"topic\", 2),\n        (\"seat\", 1),\n        (\"endpoint\", \"claude\"),\n        (\"model\", \"m-2\"),\n        (\"prompt_sha256\", hashlib.sha256(b\"other\").hexdigest()),\n    ]:\n        planned = {**k, field: other}\n        _, plan = resume(store, repo, [planned])\n        assert plan.reused == {}, field\n        assert [reason for _, reason in plan.not_reused] == [field.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")], field\n",

          "end_line": 3353,
          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_runner_holds_no_command_list_of_its_own() -> None:\n    \"\"\"`verify_all.sh` must not know the check commands itself.\n\n    This is pinned negatively: the script must contain no call of the checked\n    scripts — with exactly two exceptions, the call of `ci_gates.py`, through\n    which it obtains the list, and the measurement helper `verify_duration.py`,\n    which holds no gate command and reads no gate list; it only takes\n    monotonic readings around what the runner already executes.\n    \"\"\"\n    text = RUNNER.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    aufrufe = set(re.findall(r\"scripts/([a-z_]+\\.py)\", text))\n    assert aufrufe <= {\"ci_gates.py\", \"verify_duration.py\"}, (\n        f\"verify_all.sh calls scripts directly: {sorted(aufrufe - {'ci_gates.py', 'verify_duration.py'})}. \"\n        \"That way it holds a second list — exactly the drift it is written against.\"\n    )\n",

          "citation": "tests/test_ci.py::test_runner_report_matches_selected_job",

          "excerpt": "def test_runner_report_matches_selected_job(tmp_path: Path) -> None:\n    \"\"\"The initial report names the selected job and counts membership, not execution.\n\n    Ledger criteria 1-3 of docs-job-report-header: a report that names `verify`\n    under a docs or drift selection, confuses the subset, verify, drift and total\n    counts, changes the field set, fills candidate or base from another checkout's\n    refs, or digests other bytes than the gate file's — each goes red here. A failed gate keeps its raw exit status — an advisory failure is not a pass.\n    code, _, _ = _run(\n        capsys,\n        \"gate\",\n        \"--run\",\n        first.strip(),\n        \"--gate\",\n        \"probe\",\n        \"--start\",\n        \"0.0\",\n        \"--end\",\n        \"2.0\",\n        \"--status\",\n        \"3\",\n        \"--enforcement\",\n        \"advisory\",\n    )\n    assert code == 0\n    gates = [event for event in _history(state) if event[\"event\"] == \"gate\"]\n    assert len(gates) == 1\n    assert gates[0][\"exit\"] == 3 and gates[0][\"enforcement\"] == \"advisory\" and gates[0][\"seconds\"] == 2.0\n\n    # Planted fault: a red cheap ruff still starts `make verify`, or the attempt is accepted.\"\"\"\n    red_check = {\"stdout\": \"scripts/a.py:1:1: F401 `a` imported but unused\\n\", \"exit\": 1}\n    red_format = {\"stdout\": \"would reformat scripts/a.py\\n\", \"exit\": 1}\n    # One attempt consumes four ruff steps: the format step's check and format, then the cheap\n    # lint and format check. The red stands at the cheap position, never at the format step's.\n    steps = [{}, {}, red_check, {}] if half == \"lint\" else [{}, {}, {}, red_format]\n    venv_ruff(world)\n    baseline = git(world.root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\")\n    world.script(\n        claude=[formatted_attempt(), {\"stdout\": \"must not run\"}, {\"stdout\": \"must not run\"}],\n        ruff=steps * 3,\n        make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\\n\"}],\n    )\n    assert world.run(\"implement\") == 1\n    assert world.calls(\"make\") == [], \"a red cheap ruff still started `make verify`\"\n    assert git(world.root, \"rev-list\", \"--count\", f\"{baseline}..HEAD\") == \"0\"\n    assert CHEAP in world.text()\n",

          "excerpt": "# The verify commands live in ONE place: decisions/gates.yaml.\n# make verify delegates to the runner, the runner asks ci_gates.py, and that\n# reads the gate file. Nothing here restates a gate command — the two recipe\n# lines below exist because tests/test_ci.py pins Makefile and gate list\n# against each other (W-6).\n#\n# `make test` / `make staleness` are the two gates a developer runs by hand\n# most often; their recipes are copied verbatim from decisions/gates.yaml and\n# held there by test_the_makefile_runs_what_the_one_list_runs.\n\n# `make venv` builds this checkout's own `.venv` from the lock; `make lock`\n# writes the lock from `pyproject.toml` (bead coding-harness-ei0). The lock's\n# first lines record the exact command that wrote it, and rerunning that\n# command must give the committed file byte for byte. Only the machine that\n# changes a pin needs uv; CI and `make venv` install with pip.\n.PHONY: verify test staleness gates leakcheck venv lock change index report close-merged archive help\n\nverify:\n\tbash scripts/verify_all.sh\n\ntest:\n\tpython3 -m pytest tests/ -q -n auto\n\nstaleness:\n\tpython3 scripts/plans_registry.py --check\n\ngates:\n\tpython3 scripts/ci_gates.py --list\n\n# Runs before a foreign call (scripts/stage2.py runs it itself) and never in CI:\n# it needs the denylist each machine keeps outside the repository.\nleakcheck:\n\tpython3 scripts/leakcheck.py --name \"$(NAME)\"\n\n# The interpreter must meet `requires-python` in pyproject.toml (the one place\n# the minimum is declared). Default: the first of python3.12, python3 on PATH;\n# `make venv PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12` names one. A wrong version\n# is refused before `.venv` exists, so no half-built environment is left\n# behind (bead coding-harness-y9q).\nPYTHON ?= $(shell command -v python3.12 || command -v python3)\n\nvenv:\n\t@need=$$(sed -n 's/^requires-python *= *\">=\\([0-9.]*\\)\".*/\\1/p' pyproject.toml); \\\n\thave=$$('$(PYTHON)' -c 'import sys; print(\"%d.%d\" % sys.version_info[:2])' 2>/dev/null); \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$need\" ]; then echo \"make venv: no requires-python in pyproject.toml\" >&2; exit 1; fi; \\\n\tif [ -z \"$$have\" ] || [ \"$$(printf '%s\\n%s\\n' \"$$need\" \"$$have\" | sort -t. -k1,1n -k2,2n | head -n 1)\" != \"$$need\" ]; then \\\n\t\techo \"make venv: '$(PYTHON)' is Python $${have:-unknown}, but the lock needs $$need or newer.\" >&2; \\\n\t\techo \"Provide one, e.g.: make venv PYTHON=/opt/homebrew/bin/python3.12\" >&2; \\\n\t\texit 1; \\\n\tfi\n\t'$(PYTHON)' -m venv .venv\n\t.venv/bin/python3 -m pip install --require-hashes -r requirements-ci.txt\n\nlock:\n\tuv pip compile pyproject.toml --group dev --universal --generate-hashes --exclude-newer \"$$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT00:00:00Z)\" -o requirements-ci.txt\n\n# The entry the workflow promises (docs/WORKFLOW.md, bead coding-harness-i0l).\n# NAME and BEAD are checked on the make level — given on the command line, never\n# taken from a stray exported variable — and the recipe passes them to\n# the entry script through its exported environment — their values are never\n# interpolated into the shell line, so arguments stay data, never code.\nchange:\n\t$(if $(and $(NAME),$(filter command line,$(origin NAME))),,$(error usage: make change NAME=<name> BEAD=<existing-bead-id> — both on the command line))\n\t$(if $(and $(BEAD),$(filter command line,$(origin BEAD))),,$(error usage: make change NAME=<name> BEAD=<existing-bead-id> — both on the command line))\n\t@export NAME BEAD; python3 scripts/new_change.py \"$$NAME\" --bead \"$$BEAD\"\n\nindex:\n\t@python3 scripts/plans_registry.py --index\n\n# The run report (bead coding-harness-o2yc): one local, read-only snapshot of the\n# active changes - recorded attempts, time against the plan-card appetite, live\n# process and memory figures.           "excerpt": "def test_reuse_requires_the_exact_binding_seat_model_and_prompt(store, repo):\n    k = key(\"s1\")\n    make_source(store, repo, results=[(k, terminal(k))])\n    source, plan = resume(store, repo, [k])\n    assert source.usable and set(plan.reused) == {\"s1\"} and plan.not_reused == []\n    assert plan.reused[\"s1\"][\"report\"] == \"REPORT\"\n    for field, other in [\n        (\"stage\", \"map\"),\n        (\"topic\", 2),\n        (\"seat\", 1),\n        (\"endpoint\", \"claude\"),\n        (\"model\", \"m-2\"),\n        (\"prompt_sha256\", hashlib.sha256(b\"other\").hexdigest()),\n    ]:\n        planned = {**k, field: other}\n        _, plan = resume(store, repo, [planned])\n        assert plan.reused == {}, field\n        assert [reason for _, reason in plan.not_reused] == [field.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")], field\n",

          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_verification_admission_is_outside_execution_timeout(world: World, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch) -> None:\n    # Criterion 4 of the machine lock. Planted fault: the admission wait counted against the\n    # step limit — a short passing check times out after queueing — or the limit dropped, so\n    # a hung executing check escapes its group cleanup.\n    monkeypatch.setattr(stage2, \"VERIFY_SECONDS\", 2.0)\n    ready = world.state / \"holder-ready\"\n    holder = _real_holder(ready)\n    try:\n        _holder_acquired(ready)\n        problems: list[str] = []\n\n        def attempt() -> None:\n            problems.extend(stage2.verify_attempt(world.root, world.plan))\n\n        world.script(make=[{\"stdout\": \"green\", \"sleep\": 1.5}])\n        queued = threading.Thread(target=attempt)\n        queued.start()\n        time.sleep(1.0)  # a real second of queueing while the holder owns the admission\n        holder.terminate()\n        holder.wait(timeout=30)\n        queued.join(timeout=90)\n        assert problems == [], f\"the admission wait consumed the step limit: {problems}\"\n        assert len(world.calls(\"make\")) == 1\n    finally:\n        if holder.poll() is None:\n            holder.kill()\n            holder.wait(timeout=10)\n\n    # and the limit still binds the executing check: a hung make ends inside it\n    world.script(make=[{\"stdout\": \"too late\", \"sleep\": 30}])\n    problems = stage2.verify_attempt(world.root, world.plan)\n    assert len(problems) == 1 and \"did not finish\" in problems[0], problems\n",

Empty when all\n    applicable commands are green. A command with no target is skipped (spec,\n    criterion 4); a red, an unstartable or an over-bound command returns that one bounded,\n    protected diagnostic and the attempt ends before derived preparation and `make verify` (spec,\n    criteria 1, 2 and 10). The ledger references come from `accepted_plan` - the accepted plan's\n    snapshot; without one the working plan stands in, as a direct `verify_attempt` call does.\n    \"\"\"\n    try:\n        targets = format_targets(root, env)\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        lines = protect_diagnostics(f\"the cheap lint targets could not be listed: {error}\", key).splitlines()\n        return [\"\\n\".join(_shrink(lines, TAIL_LINES))]\n    if targets:\n        problem = _cheap_ruff(root, env, key, targets)\n        if problem:\n            return [problem]\n    if accepted_plan is None:\n        try:\n            accepted_plan = plan.read_bytes()\n        except OSError as error:\n            return [protect_diagnostics(f\"the accepted plan could not be read for the cheap tests: {error}\", key)]\n    tests, fault = selected_tests(root, env, accepted_plan, previous)\n    if fault is not None:\n        lines = protect_diagnostics(f\"the cheap tests could not be selected: {fault}\", key).splitlines()\n        return [\"\\n\".join(_shrink(lines, TAIL_LINES))]\n    if not tests:\n        return []",

          "excerpt": "def cmd_start(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create one run identity and append its start record with the machine context.\"\"\"\n    memory = verify_lock.read_available_memory()\n    porcelain = _git([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n    event = {\n        \"v\": EVENT_VERSION,\n        \"event\": RUN_START,\n        \"run_id\": uuid.uuid4().hex,\n        \"utc\": _utc_now(),\n        \"repository\": str(Path.cwd()),\n        \"commit\": _git([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"]),\n        # None means git could not answer; only an answer decides yes or no.\n        \"dirty\": None if porcelain is None else bool(porcelain),\n        \"config_sha256\": _gate_file_digest(),\n        \"job\": args.job,\n        \"placement\": args.placement,\n        \"memory_pct\": memory,\n        \"workers\": _worker_setting(),\n        **_context_fields(),\n    }\n    append_event(event)\n    print(event[\"run_id\"])\n    return 0\n",

          "end_line": 180,
          "excerpt": "def append_event(event: dict) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Append one complete JSON line under a file lock, so concurrent runs never mix identities.\"\"\"\n    line = json.dumps(event, sort_keys=True) + \"\\n\"\n    fd = _open_history()\n    try:\n        fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_EX)\n        try:\n            data = line.encode(\"utf-8\")\n            if os.write(fd, data) != len(data):\n                raise StorageUnusable(\"the history write was incomplete; refusing to claim a complete event\")\n        finally:\n            fcntl.flock(fd, fcntl.LOCK_UN)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the history lock or write failed ({error}); refusing to record event\") from error\n    finally:\n        os.close(fd)\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_records_bind_results_to_revision_and_configuration(\n    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A record names its commit, dirty state, gate configuration, job and the command's raw exit.\n\n    Fault this pins: runs of different jobs or dirty trees becoming\n    indistinguishable, or a failed command losing its exit status in history.\n    \"\"\"\n    state = tmp_path / \"state\"\n    repo = tmp_path / \"repo\"\n    (repo / \"decisions\").mkdir(parents=True)\n    gate_file = repo / \"decisions\" / \"gates.yaml\"\n    gate_file.write_text(\"gates: []\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    monkeypatch.chdir(repo)\n\n    commits = iter([\"a\" * 40, \"b\" * 40])\n    porcelains = iter([\"\", \" M scripts/x.py\"])\n\n    def fake_git(arguments: list[str]) -> str | None:\n        if arguments == [\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"]:\n            return next(commits, None)\n        if arguments == [\"status\", \"--porcelain\"]:\n            return next(porcelains, None)\n        return None\n\n    monkeypatch.setattr(verify_duration, \"_git\", fake_git)\n\n    code, first, _ = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"verify\", \"--placement\", \"local\")\n    assert code == 0\n    started = _history(state)[-1]\n    assert started[\"run_id\"] == first.strip()\n    assert started[\"commit\"] == \"a\" * 40 and started[\"dirty\"] is False\n    assert started[\"config_sha256\"] == hashlib.sha256(gate_file.read_bytes()).hexdigest()\n    assert started[\"repository\"] == str(repo)\n    assert started[\"utc\"].endswith(\"+00:00\"), started[\"utc\"]\n\n    code, second, _ = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"docs\", \"--placement\", \"ci\")\n    assert code == 0\n    started = _history(state)[-1]\n    assert started[\"commit\"] == \"b\" * 40 and started[\"dirty\"] is True, (\n        \"a dirty tree must be distinguishable from a clean one\"\n    )\n\n    # A failed gate keeps its raw exit status — an advisory failure is not a pass.\n    code, _, _ = _run(\n        capsys,\n        \"gate\",\n        \"--run\",\n        first.strip(),\n        \"--gate\",\n        \"probe\",\n        \"--start\",\n        \"0.0\",\n        \"--end\",\n        \"2.0\",\n        \"--status\",\n        \"3\",\n        \"--enforcement\",\n        \"advisory\",\n    )\n    assert code == 0\n  ",

          "citation": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py::plan_reuse",
          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py",
          "reference": "plan_reuse",
          "start_line": 483,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false

          "excerpt": "def test_reuse_requires_the_exact_binding_seat_model_and_prompt(store, repo):\n    k = key(\"s1\")\n    make_source(store, repo, results=[(k, terminal(k))])\n    source, plan = resume(store, repo, [k])\n    assert source.usable and set(plan.reused) == {\"s1\"} and plan.not_reused == []\n    assert plan.reused[\"s1\"][\"report\"] == \"REPORT\"\n    for field, other in [\n        (\"stage\", \"map\"),\n        (\"topic\", 2),\n        (\"seat\", 1),\n        (\"endpoint\", \"claude\"),\n        (\"model\", \"m-2\"),\n        (\"prompt_sha256\", hashlib.sha256(b\"other\").hexdigest()),\n    ]:\n        planned = {**k, field: other}\n        _, plan = resume(store, repo, [planned])\n        assert plan.reused == {}, field\n        assert [reason for _, reason in plan.not_reused] == [field.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")], field\n",

New\n    files are added intent-to-add for the gates and dropped afterwards; a refusal of the admission,\n    a timeout and a red exit are problems; a `make` that cannot be started raises `CallFailed`.\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission([\"make\", \"verify\"]) as owned:\n            try:\n                intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n            except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n                return [f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before `make verify`: {error}\"]\n            done = launch(\n                [\"make\", \"verify\"],\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except verify_lock.VerifyLockError as error:\n        problems.append(scrub(f\"`make verify` was not started: {error}\", key))\n    except StepTimedOut as error:\n        problems.append(f\"`make verify` did not finish: {error}\")\n    else:\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            problems.append(f\"`make verify` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after `make verify`: {error}\")\n    return problems\n",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def verify_draft(\n    root: Path, ctx: Context, key: str | None, new_adrs: list[str], tools: dict[str, str] | None = None\n) -> tuple[list[str], bool]:\n    \"\"\"A draft attempt's post-run checks: the problems, and whether the answer is owed.\n\n    The order is the spec's (criteria 10 to 16): the ADR count, the derived files, the document check\n    `bash scripts/verify_all.sh --job docs` - its exit code decides; the one missing answer it tolerates\n    is the gate's own, asked for through `check_adr_answers.TOLERATE_ENV`, never read from its output -\n    the two artefacts, the plan card and the `## Time used` heading. Implement keeps full `make verify`;\n    repair takes the targeted check, with the full suite as its fallback and before phase 6.\n    \"\"\"\n    owed = False\n    if len(new_adrs) > 1:\n        problems = [\"the attempt left more than one new ADR file: \" + \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in new_adrs)]\n        return problems, owed\n    tampered = tool_problem(root, tools)\n    if tampered:\n        return [tampered], owed\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n                # The one tolerance of a draft is the gate's own, set by this runner alone: with this\n                # variable `adr-answers` reports this change's missing answer and passes, so the\n                # exit code of the document check decides and no output is read (spec, criterion 13; F-9, F-10).\n                check_adr_answers.TOLERATE_ENV: ctx.change,\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n    preparation = prepare_derived(root, env, key)\n    if preparation:\n        return preparation, owed\n    try:\n        # One machine-wide admission before the timed check: queue and memory waits consume no\n        # step limit; a refusal is a failed check, never a started one (bead coding-harness-p6mu).\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission(DOCS_VERIFY) as owned:\n            done = launch(\n                DOCS_VERIFY,\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except (CallFailed, verify_lock.VerifyLockError) as error:\n        # A document check that cannot start is as failed a post-run check as a red one: its\n        # diagnostics reach the attempt's block, and the chain moves on to the next attempt (2a's F-7).\n        return [f\"`{DOCS_VERIFY_NAME}` could not run: {error}\"], owed\n    problems = []\n    if done.returncode != 0:\n        problems.append(f\"`{DOCS_VERIFY_NAME}` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    else:\n        owed = answer_is_owed(root, ctx.change)\n    plan_missing = not ctx.plan.is_file()\n    for name in (\"spec.md\", \"plan.md\"):\n        if not (ctx.folder / name).is_file():\n            problems.append(f\"plans/changes/{ctx.change}/{name} is missing after the draft.\")\n    if not plan_missing:\n        # An absent plan.md is one problem of its own: the card and Time-used checks would read an\n        # empty string and name two faults a missing file cannot have (repair L3-4).\n        plan_text = _read_quietly(ctx.plan)\n        if card_problem(plan_text) is not None:\n            problems.append(CARD_PROBLEM)\n        if not TIME_HEADING.search(plan_text):\n            problems.append(f\"plans/changes/{ctx.change}/plan.md has no `## Time used` heading.\")\n    return problems, owed\n",

          "excerpt": "def _open_history() -> int:\n    \"\"\"A private regular history file for appending; an aliased or nonregular destination refuses.\n\n    The same shape as the admission's lock files: the no-follow open fails on\n    a symlink standing in the file's place, a FIFO cannot pass the regular\n    check, and nothing is ever written through a substituted destination.\n    \"\"\"\n    root = verify_lock.state_root()\n    try:\n        root.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(\n            f\"the shared state directory {root} cannot be created ({error.strerror or error})\"\n        ) from error\n    if root.is_symlink() or not root.is_dir():\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the shared state directory {root} is not a usable directory\")\n    path = history_path()\n    try:\n        return os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_APPEND | os.O_NOFOLLOW, 0o600)\n    except FileExistsError:\n        pass\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(\n            f\"the history file {path} cannot be created no-follow ({error.strerror or error}) — \"\n            \"a substituted destination is refused, never written through\"\n        ) from error\n    # O_NONBLOCK so a FIFO standing in the file's place is refused below, never waited on.\n    try:\n        fd = os.open(path, os.O_WRONLY | os.O_APPEND | os.O_NOFOLLOW | os.O_NONBLOCK)\n    except OSError as error:\n        raise StorageUnusable(\n            f\"the history file {path} is not a private regular file; refusing substituted history\"\n        ) from error\n    info = os.fstat(fd)\n    if not stat.S_ISREG(info.st_mode) or info.st_nlink != 1:\n        os.close(fd)\n        raise StorageUnusable(f\"the history file {path} is not an unaliased regular file; refusing substituted history\")\n    return fd\n",

          "excerpt": "def test_history_rejects_substituted_destinations(\n    tmp_path: Path, monkeypatch: pytest.MonkeyPatch, capsys: pytest.CaptureFixture[str]\n) -> None:\n    \"\"\"A symlink or FIFO standing where the history belongs refuses; nothing is written through it.\n\n    Fault this pins: an append following a substituted file to its target, a\n    FIFO in the file's place hanging the runner, or an aliased state root\n    being written into at all.\n    \"\"\"\n    root = tmp_path / \"state\" / \"coding-harness\"\n    root.mkdir(parents=True)\n\n    # A symlink in the file's place: the victim keeps its bytes, the op refuses.\n    victim = tmp_path / \"victim.jsonl\"\n    victim.write_text(\"do not write through me\\n\", encoding=\"utf-8\")\n    (root / verify_duration.HISTORY_NAME).symlink_to(victim)\n    code, _, err = _run(capsys, \"start\", \"--job\", \"verify\", \"--placement\", \"local\")\n    assert code == 2 and \"substituted\" in err, err\n    assert victim.read_text(encoding=\"utf-8\") == \"do not write through me\\n\"\n\n    #           "excerpt": "def hold_admission(command: list[str]) -> Iterator[int | None]:\n    \"\"\"One machine admission around protected work: queue, memory gate, published ownership.\n\n    Yields the lock descriptor local children must inherit, or None when this\n    entry is nested in an ancestor's admission.           "excerpt": "dur_call() {\n    local _target=\"$1\"; shift\n    local _out=\"\"\n    if [ \"$DUR_BROKEN\" -eq 1 ]; then\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    if ! _out=$(\"$PYTHON\" -m scripts.verify_duration \"$@\"); then\n        echo \"verify-duration: measurement storage unusable — this run is not recorded; gates and verdicts continue unchanged\" >&2\n        DUR_BROKEN=1\n        printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"\"\n        return 1\n    fi\n    printf -v \"$_target\" %s \"$_out\"\n}\nduration_placement=local\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && duration_placement=ci\ndur_call exec_t0 clock\ndur_call RUN_ID start --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$duration_placement\"\n\n# The report binds the verdict to a state of the world: which commit ran,\n# against which base, with which gate configuration.\n\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --report --job \"$JOB\" || exit 2\n\n# Die Gate-Liste wird ZUERST geholt und ihr Fehlschlag ist fatal: ein Lauf\n# ueber null gemessene Gates darf nicht in einem gruenen Urteil enden\n# (Runner-Review 2026-09-21, PR #11). --placement lokal: hosted-only Gates\n# misst nur die CI — der lokale Lauf laesst sie deklariert aus (bead 1jg.2),\n# die Gate-Datei nennt das placement, nicht der Zufall. --ci misst dagegen\n# denselben Satz wie die abgeleitete Workflow (--placement ci): wer den\n# Runner in der gehosteten CI aufruft, darf dort nicht ploetzlich ohne die\n# hosted-Gates dastehen (Befund 2 an bead coding-harness-1jg.3, Review von\n# PR #32). Die Action-Entsprechungen sind dabei REPORT, niemals stilles\n# Auslassen.\nplatzierung=lokal\n[ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && platzierung=ci\ngate_tsv=$(\"$PYTHON\" scripts/ci_gates.py --commands --job \"$JOB\" --placement \"$platzierung\" --tsv $([ \"$CI_MODE\" -eq 1 ] && echo \"--skip-equivalents\")) \\\n    || { echo \"die Gate-Liste liess sich nicht erzeugen — kein VERIFY ohne gemessene Gates\" >&2; exit 2; }\n[ -n \"$gate_tsv\" ] || { echo \"die Gate-Liste ist leer — ein Job ohne messbare Gates ist ein Konfigurationsfehler\" >&2; exit 2; }\n\necho \"\"\necho \"── gates: job=$JOB ──────────────────────────────────────────────\"\n\n# The commands come out of the one list — id, enforcement, command, per tab.\n# The runner respects the vocabulary: only `block` turns the run red,\n# `report`/`advisory` speak up without blocking.\nfehler=0\nstop_gate=\"\"\nverbleibend=\"\"\nwhile IFS=\"$(printf '\\t')\" read -r gid enf cmd; do\n    [ -z \"$cmd\" ] && continue\n    # Cheap-first stop (bead coding-harness-bxxt.1): after the first blocking\n    # failure no further selected gate runs. The remaining ids are collected\n    # from the already obtained TSV and named in one summary below the loop;\n    # `--ci` never sets stop_gate and keeps running every selected gate.\n    if [ \"$CI_MODE\" -ne 1 ] && [ -n \"$stop_gate\" ]; then\n        verbleibend=\"${verbleibend}${gid}\n\"\n        continue\n    fi\n    # Werkzeuge aus dem Pin aufloesen (gates.md G-12): `python3` in der Liste\n    # heisst \"der gepinnte Interpreter\", nicht \"was der PATH gerade hergibt\".\n    # Die CI macht dasselbe ueber setup-python mit derselben Version.\n    # Quoted for `sh -c`: an absolute path may hold a space; a quote inside it is escaped.\n    python_word=\"'$(printf %s \"$PYTHON\" | sed \"s/'/'\\\\\\\\''/g\")'\"\n    lauf_cmd=${cmd/python3/\"$python_word\"}\n    echo \"\"\n    # Keep machine-local interpreter paths out of logs and repair evidence.\n    echo \"── [$gid] $ $cmd\"\n    # Monotonic readings immediately around the unchanged gate command; the\n    # raw status is captured before any timing operation, so it is the gate\n    # command's own and not a helper's (bead coding-harness-1um6).\n    g_secs=\"\"\n    dur_call g_t0 clock\n    sh -c \"$lauf_cmd\"\n    gate_status=$?\n    dur_call g_t1 clock\n    if [ -n \"$RUN_ID\" ] && [ -n \"$g_t0\" ] && [ -n \"$g_t1\" ]; then\n        dur_call g_secs gate --run \"$RUN_ID\" --gate \"$gid\" --start \"$g_t0\" --end \"$g_t1\" --status \"$gate_status\" --enforcement \"$enf\"\n    fi\n    if [ \"$gate_status\" -eq 0 ]; then\n        echo \"── [$gid] gruen\"\n    elif [ \"$enf\" = \"block\" ]; then\n        fehler=1\n        # `--ci` stays exhaust",

          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",

          "excerpt": "def cmd_start(args: argparse.Namespace) -> int:\n    \"\"\"Create one run identity and append its start record with the machine context.\"\"\"\n    memory = verify_lock.read_available_memory()\n    porcelain = _git([\"status\", \"--porcelain\"])\n    event = {\n        \"v\": EVENT_VERSION,\n        \"event\": RUN_START,\n        \"run_id\": uuid.uuid4().hex,\n        \"utc\": _utc_now(),\n        \"repository\": str(Path.cwd()),\n        \"commit\": _git([\"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\"]),\n        # None means git could not answer; only an answer decides yes or no.\n        \"dirty\": None if porcelain is None else bool(porcelain),\n        \"config_sha256\": _gate_file_digest(),\n        \"job\": args.job,\n        \"placement\": args.placement,\n        \"memory_pct\": memory,\n        \"workers\": _worker_setting(),\n        **_context_fields(),\n    }\n    append_event(event)\n    print(event[\"run_id\"])\n    return 0\n",

          "citation": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md::The target picture",
          "end_line": 181,
          "excerpt": "## The target picture\n\nThis is the usual layering of checks in larger code bases — fast checks near\nthe edit, the full suite once before integration on shared infrastructure,\nresults reused when inputs did not change, a time budget that is enforced.\nIt is stated here from general knowledge; **no outside source was read for\nthis note** — the literature belongs to the testing-strategy research\n(coding-harness-1ga5).\n\n| Layer | When | Budget (proposal) | What runs | Where |\n|---|---|---|---|---|\n| 1 · Formalities | after every runner attempt, before anything else | seconds | formatter, linter, front matter, question context, registry | local, no lock |\n| 2 · Targeted | after every implement, draft and repair attempt | under 2 minutes | the tests the change touches and names | local, no lock |\n| 3 · Full | once per change before phase 6; again only when the tree changed | under 10 minutes of execution | every gate | hosted CI first; the local slots as fallback |\n| 4 · Merge | on the pull request and in the merge queue | as layer 3 | every gate | hosted CI (today already) |\n\nFour rules hold the picture together:\n\n- **A full result is reused.** A green full check is recorded under a key\n  made from the tree content, the gate file and the lock file. Phase 6, the\n  orchestrator and a rerun ask for the key first. Today the review verb runs\n  its own full check on a tree the orchestrator has just checked.\n- **The suite has a budget.** A number for the full check (proposal: 10\n  minutes of execution on this machine) and one per test (proposal: 5 s\n  without a marker). A change that breaks the budget either speeds something\n  up or moves tests into a slower, rarer layer — decided in the pull request,\n  not silently.\n- **Full runs per change are counted.** Target: three or fewer (attempt\n  accepted, phase 6, pull request); today the median is seven.\n- **Capacity comes from outside.** The repository is public, so hosted\n  runs cost nothing and run side by side (bead coding-harness-u3qg). The\n  local machine keeps layers 1 and 2, which need no lock.\n\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "docs/research/2026-11-09-make-verify-long-term.md",
          "reference": "The target picture",
          "start_line": 149,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        },

A path deleted on disk is absent; a link, or a file whose\n    real path leaves the worktree, is never read. A source that cannot be read raises\n    `CannotMeasure`, so a caller never mistakes an unreadable inventory for zero links.\n    \"\"\"\n\n    def __init__(self, repo: str, *, env: dict[str, str] | None = None, timeout: int = 120) -> None:\n        self.env = env\n        self.timeout = timeout\n        self.repo = repo\n        self.rev = \"worktree\"\n        self._blobs: dict[str, str] = {}  # path -> path, regular files only\n        self._read: dict[str, S",

          "excerpt": "def require_fresh_full_verification(root: Path, change: str) -> None:\n    \"\"\"Phase 6's boundary: a fresh green full `make verify` of the current head, before any reviewer call.\n\n    A repair's targeted check never stands for it (bead coding-harness-gxwg). The tree must be the\n    committed head, except runner call audit lines and their current-date header stamp in\n    this change's `findings.md` outside byte-identical phase-6 blocks. Review reads its phase and\n    session markers before the runner writes any audit. The head, index and tree must be the same\n    after the check as before.\n    The check runs on every phase-6 invocation, a re-check included, and leaves no receipt: it\n    measures the head being reviewed.\n    A dirty tree or a changed head or tree refuses; a red, unstartable or timed-out check fails the call.\n    \"\"\"\n    env = runner_env(\n        foreign_env(\n            {\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_COUNT\": \"1\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_KEY_0\": \"commit.gpgsign\",\n                \"GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0\": \"false\",\n            }\n        ),\n        root,\n    )\n\n    def standing() -> tuple[str, list[str], tuple[bytes, bytes] | None]:\n        head = _git_output(root, \"rev-parse\", \"HEAD\", env=env).strip()\n        dirty = sorted(path.as_posix() for path in changed_paths(root, env=env))\n        audit = None\n        name = f\"plans/changes/{change}/findings.md\"\n        path = root / name\n        if name in dirty and path.is_file() and not path.is_symlink() and not path.stat().st_mode & 0o111:\n            committed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\"{head}:{name}\", env=env)\n            indexed = _git_bytes(root, \"show\", f\":{name}\", env=env)\n            content = path.read_bytes()\n            entries = _git_output(root, \"ls-files\", \"--stage\", \"--\", name, env=env)\n            if entries.startswith(\"100644 \") and all(review_audit_only(committed, body) for body in (indexed, content)):\n                dirty.remove(name)\n                audit = (indexed, content)\n        return head, dirty, audit\n\n    try:\n        head, dirty, audit = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the current head could not be read for the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if dirty:\n        listing = \", \".join(f\"`{path}`\" for path in dirty[:20])\n        raise Refused(\n            f\"phase 6 reviews a committed tree for `{change}`, and these paths differ from HEAD: {listing}; commit or put \"\n            \"them back, then run review again. No reviewer was called.\"\n        )\n    problems = full_verify(root, env, None)\n    if problems:\n        raise CallFailed(\n            \"the full `make verify` before phase 6 did not pass; no reviewer was called:\\n\" + \"\\n\".join(problems)\n        )\n    try:\n        after = standing()\n    except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n        raise Refused(f\"the head could not be read after the full check before phase 6 ({error})\") from error\n    if after != (head, dirty, audit):\n        raise CallFailed(\n            f\"the head or the tree changed while the full check before phase 6 ran (HEAD {head[:12]}); \"\n            \"no reviewer was called. Run review again.\"\n        )\n    print(f\"review: full `make verify` green on {head[:12]} before the reviewer starts\")\n",

          "excerpt": "def full_verify(root: Path, env: dict[str, str], key: str | None) -> list[str]:\n    \"\"\"`make verify` under one machine admission: the problems, empty when it is green.\n\n    The full check of a repair whose targeted coverage was not safe, and of phase 6's boundary. New\n    files are added intent-to-add for the gates and dropped afterwards; a refusal of the admission,\n    a timeout and a red exit are problems; a `make` that cannot be started raises `CallFailed`.\n    \"\"\"\n    problems: list[str] = []\n    intended: list[bytes] = []\n    try:\n        with verify_lock.hold_admission([\"make\", \"verify\"]) as owned:\n            try:\n                intended = intend_new_files(root, env)\n            except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n                return [f\"the attempt's new files could not be added intent-to-add before `make verify`: {error}\"]\n            done = launch(\n                [\"make\", \"verify\"],\n                root,\n                verify_lock.inherit_env(env),\n                timeout=VERIFY_SECONDS,\n                limit=f\"the runner's step limit after {VERIFY_SECONDS // 60} minutes\",\n                pass_fds=_lock_fds(owned),\n            )\n    except verify_lock.VerifyLockError as error:\n        problems.append(scrub(f\"`make verify` was not started: {error}\", key))\n    except StepTimedOut as error:\n        problems.append(f\"`make verify` did not finish: {error}\")\n    else:\n        if done.returncode != 0:\n            problems.append(f\"`make verify` exited {done.returncode}\\n{verify_evidence(done, key)}\".rstrip())\n    finally:\n        try:\n            drop_intended(root, intended, env)\n        except (Refused, OSError) as error:\n            problems.append(f\"the attempt's intent-to-add entries could not be removed after `make verify`: {error}\")\n    return problems\n",

          "excerpt": "def hold_admission(command: list[str]) -> Iterator[int | None]:\n    \"\"\"One machine admission around protected work: queue, memory gate, published ownership.\n\n    Yields the lock descriptor local children must inherit, or None when this\n    entry is nested in an ancestor's admission. Refusals raise\n    VerifyLockRefused or MemoryFloorRefused before the body runs; release\n    happens in every ending, after any child cleanup the caller does.\n    \"\"\"\n    inherited = nested_holder_pid()\n    if inherited is not None:\n        _log(f\"inheriting admission from pid {inherited}; no queue and no memory wait\")\n        yield None\n        return\n    admission = _Admission(_prepare_state(), command)\n    try:\n        admission.enter()\n    except BaseException:\n        admission.release()\n        raise\n    try:\n        yield admission.state.lock_fd\n    finally:\n        admission.release()\n",

          "end_line": 519,
          "excerpt": "def plan_reuse(source, planned, validate):\n    \"\"\"Split the planned slots (dicts with ``slot_id`` and the key fields) into reused and to-launch.\n\n    ``validate(record)`` is the new run's own report validation. Every stored result that is not\n    reused is named with its reason, so a silent discard cannot happen.\n    \"\"\"\n    planned = list(planned)\n    # Results stay stored because a reverted edit may match again (design.md), but only the latest run is a\n    # source: an older run's results are named, never silently passed over (deep review RS-2-4).\n    older = [\n        (f\"{slot_id} (run {run_id})\", \"not the latest run\")\n        for run_id, slots in source.older.items()\n        for slot_id in slots\n    ]\n    if not source.usable:\n        unusable = [(slot_id, \"source run unusable\") for slot_id in sorted(source.results)]\n        return ReusePlan({}, unusable + older, planned)\n    reused, named = {}, []\n    ids = {slot[\"slot_id\"] for slot in planned}\n    for slot in planned:\n        record = source.results.get(slot[\"slot_id\"])\n        if record is None:\n            if slot[\"slot_id\"] in source.interrupted:\n                named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"interrupted\"))\n            continue\n        mismatch = next((name for name in SLOT_KEY_FIELDS if record.get(name) != slot.get(name)), None)\n        if mismatch is not None:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], mismatch.replace(\"_sha256\", \"\")))\n        elif record.get(\"outcome\") != REUSABLE_OUTCOME:\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"outcome\"))\n        elif not _valid(validate, record):\n            named.append((slot[\"slot_id\"], \"validation\"))\n        else:\n            reused[slot[\"slot_id\"]] = record\n    for slot_id in sorted(set(source.results) - ids):\n        named.append((slot_id, \"not planned\"))\n    return ReusePlan(reused, named + older, [slot for slot in planned if slot[\"slot_id\"] not in reused])\n",
          "kind": "local",
          "path": "scripts/stage2_research_store.py",
          "reference": "plan_reuse",
          "start_line": 483,
          "supported": true,
          "truncated": false
        }
